denial.reason_text: Conservative therapy requirement not met. The records do not document at least 6 weeks of physical therapy or a supervised home exercise program.

bases.title: Low back pain with or without leg symptoms

requirements.text: Symptoms present for at least 6 weeks
requirements.policy_text: Symptoms have been present for at least 6 weeks.

evidence.quote: Symptoms have now been present for about 8 weeks, with onset on 08/10/2026.
evidence.rationale: The treating physician states on 10/06/2026 that symptoms have lasted about 8 weeks, with a documented onset date.

near_misses.quote: Low back pain began about 08/10/2026 after he lifted a pallet at work.
near_misses.why_not: This gives only the onset date, in a note written about two weeks after onset, so it does not show a duration of 6 weeks by itself.

near_misses.quote: Right-sided low back pain with leg symptoms for 3 weeks.
near_misses.why_not: This states the duration as of the 09/01/2026 physical therapy evaluation, which is a past point in time and under 6 weeks.

near_misses.quote: Return in 6 weeks, sooner for leg weakness or bladder symptoms.
near_misses.why_not: The 6 weeks here is a follow-up interval in the plan, not a duration of symptoms.

requirements.text: At least 6 weeks of PT or supervised home exercise, within 3 months before request
requirements.policy_text: The member completed at least 6 weeks of physical therapy or a supervised home exercise program within the 3 months before the request.

evidence.quote: The patient attended 8 of 12 planned visits between 09/01/2026 and 09/29/2026, a period of 4 weeks.
evidence.rationale: The PT discharge note documents the therapy actually completed (8 visits over 4 weeks) and the dates it took place, shortly before the 10/06/2026 MRI order.

near_misses.quote: Physical therapy 2 visits per week for 6 weeks (12 visits).
near_misses.why_not: This is the planned course of care at the initial evaluation, not therapy completed, and the discharge note shows only 4 weeks were done.

near_misses.quote: He says he has done his home exercises most days since leaving physical therapy.
near_misses.why_not: This is the patient's own report of an unsupervised home program with no duration or clinician verification, so it does not show a supervised home exercise program of 6 weeks.

near_misses.quote: Right lumbar radiculopathy, persistent after medication and physical therapy.
near_misses.why_not: The assessment mentions physical therapy but gives no duration or dates, so it cannot show 6 weeks were completed.

quantity_check.label: physical therapy or supervised home exercise program completed

gap.what_would_satisfy: A clinician's documentation of at least 6 weeks of physical therapy or a supervised home exercise program within the 3 months before the request, such as additional PT visits or dated clinician follow-up of the home program that brings the supervised total to 6 weeks or more.
gap.suggested_action: Ask Stride Physical Therapy (Carlos Mendes, PT) whether any further supervised sessions or home-program check-ins after 09/29/2026 are documented. Ask Dr. Ashworth's office whether she supervised or monitored the home exercise program, and request any such records.

requirements.text: At least 4 weeks of anti-inflammatory or analgesic medication, unless contraindicated
requirements.policy_text: The member completed a trial of an anti-inflammatory or analgesic medication for at least 4 weeks, unless contraindicated.

evidence.quote: He has taken naproxen 500 mg twice daily for six weeks with minimal relief.
evidence.rationale: The treating physician's 10/06/2026 note documents a completed naproxen course (an anti-inflammatory) of six weeks' duration.

near_misses.quote: Start naproxen 500 mg twice daily with food.
near_misses.why_not: This is a plan to begin naproxen on 08/24/2026 and does not document how long it was taken.

near_misses.quote: He took a few doses of over-the-counter ibuprofen with little effect.
near_misses.why_not: Only a few doses of ibuprofen are reported, with no duration, so this is not a trial of at least 4 weeks.

near_misses.quote: Right lumbar radiculopathy, persistent after medication and physical therapy.
near_misses.why_not: It refers to medication generally and gives no drug or duration.

requirements.text: Re-evaluation after conservative therapy shows symptoms persist
requirements.policy_text: A clinical re-evaluation after conservative therapy documents persistent symptoms.

evidence.quote: Re-evaluation after conservative therapy: right-sided low back and leg pain persists at 6 out of 10 with no meaningful improvement.
evidence.rationale: The treating physician's 10/06/2026 visit note is labelled a re-evaluation after conservative therapy and states that the pain persists without meaningful improvement.

near_misses.quote: Leg symptoms unchanged. Minimal overall change.
near_misses.why_not: This is the physical therapist's discharge status, not a clinician re-evaluation after the full course of conservative therapy, though it supports the persistence of symptoms.

requirements.text: Record documents a red-flag condition, waiving criteria 3.1(a) through (d)
requirements.policy_text: the record documents any of the following: progressive motor weakness; bowel or bladder dysfunction or saddle anesthesia; or suspected cancer, infection, or fracture.

near_misses.quote: He denies bowel or bladder dysfunction, fever, and unexplained weight loss, and has no history of cancer.
near_misses.why_not: The most recent exam states that bowel or bladder dysfunction, fever, weight loss and cancer history are absent, so none of the listed red flags is documented.

near_misses.quote: Strength is 5/5 in both legs. No saddle anesthesia.
near_misses.why_not: Strength is normal, so there is no motor weakness, and saddle anesthesia is explicitly absent.

near_misses.quote: Sensation is mildly reduced over the outer right foot. Ankle reflex slightly reduced on the right.
near_misses.why_not: These are mild sensory and reflex findings consistent with radiculopathy. They are not progressive motor weakness, bowel or bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, or suspected cancer, infection or fracture.

gap.summary: No red flag under §3.2 is documented: the record explicitly denies bowel or bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, fever, weight loss and cancer history, shows normal 5/5 strength, and shows no fracture on X-ray.
gap.what_would_satisfy: A clinician note documenting progressive motor weakness, bowel or bladder dysfunction or saddle anesthesia, or a suspected cancer, infection or fracture, if any of these is actually present.
gap.suggested_action: Ask Dr. Ashworth whether any §3.2 red-flag finding was present but not recorded, for example new or worsening weakness. If none was, the request should rely on another pathway, such as persistent radiculopathy after about 6 weeks of conservative therapy, rather than on a red flag.

recommendation.banner: Evidence incomplete for §3.1(b): 4 of 6 weeks documented. No alternative basis is supported by this record. Obtain the missing documentation before appealing.
recommendation.rationale: Neither the stated basis nor any alternative basis in the policy is fully supported by the record.
human_actions: Ask Stride Physical Therapy (Carlos Mendes, PT) whether any further supervised sessions or home-program check-ins after 09/29/2026 are documented. Ask Dr. Ashworth's office whether she supervised or monitored the home exercise program, and request any such records.
Do not submit an appeal until the gap is documented.

blocks.text: The record documents that symptoms have been present for about 8 weeks, with onset on 08/10/2026.
The record documents that he has taken naproxen 500 mg twice daily for six weeks with minimal relief.
The record documents that on re-evaluation after conservative therapy, right-sided low back and leg pain persists at 6 out of 10 with no meaningful improvement.
§3.1(b): 4 of 6 weeks documented. This paragraph cannot be written until it is documented.
